title: Ghost Interviewer Locks the Door to Its API Key | vitalii.no
description:
How a single shared API key behind a live AI interview tool went from "anyone who finds the URL" to a strict email allow-list, checked three times over.

Ghost Interviewer runs on one shared API key, and the only thing standing between a stranger and that key was knowing the sign-in URL. Any Google account could open a session and start spending real API credits, with no list of who was actually allowed in.

The app now checks every Google sign-in against an explicit allow-list before a session is ever created, rejecting anyone not on it. The same list is checked again on the raw token exchange, and once more on every later request carrying an already-issued session token — a leaked or forged token from an unlisted address is worthless at every layer.

Tested by signing in with a second personal Google account not on the list: all three checks rejected it.
